summary: Describes simpler module debugging: use madbg (or another remote debugger) with set_trace and madbg connect, the q library, or raise an Exception with the value since print() doesn't work in modules.
questions: How can I attach a debugger to an Ansible module running on a remote host?
Why doesn't print() show anything from my module?
What's a quick way to see a variable's value inside a module?

answer_card.title: Simple module debugging
answer_card.answer_md:
- Add `import madbg; madbg.set_trace()` at the breakpoint and run `madbg connect` (open the port through any firewall for remote nodes). Other remote debuggers may work but aren't guaranteed.
- The `q` library is also handy.
- `print()` doesn't work in modules; use `raise Exception(some_value)` and Ansible will show the message on the control node.
